/research/commercial-yields-capital-valu.title: Commercial Yields & Capital Values | Valunxt
/research/commercial-yields-capital-valu.desc: A data-led read on office, retail, and warehousing yields, rental growth, and capital values across key markets.
/research/commercial-yields-capital-valu.body: wp-singular page-template-default page page-id-9114 page-parent wp-custom-logo wp-embed-responsive wp-theme-execor full header-layout-logo-menu no-page-header no-middle-header responsive-layout vamtam-is-elementor elementor-active elementor-pro-active vamtam-wc-cart-empty wc-product-gallery-slider-active vamtam-font-smoothing layout-full elementor-default elementor-kit-5 elementor-page elementor-page-9114
/research/commercial-yields-capital-valu.intro: A data-led read on office, retail, and warehousing across our core markets. We examine the spread between yields and capital values, the trajectory of rental growth, and where repricing is creating opportunities for investors focused on durable, contracted income.
takeaways: Grade-A office yields are stabilising as leasing holds up and quality supply stays constrained.
Warehousing and logistics continue to benefit from structural demand and resilient rental growth.
Retail is bifurcating, with prime, experience-led assets outperforming secondary locations.
The spread between yields and capital values is opening selective, income-focused entry points.

/research/dubai-residential-market-revie.title: Dubai Residential Market Review | Valunxt
/research/dubai-residential-market-revie.desc: Supply, absorption, and pricing trends across Dubai's prime and mid-market residential communities.
/research/dubai-residential-market-revie.body: wp-singular page-template-default page page-id-9112 page-parent wp-custom-logo wp-embed-responsive wp-theme-execor full header-layout-logo-menu no-page-header no-middle-header responsive-layout vamtam-is-elementor elementor-active elementor-pro-active vamtam-wc-cart-empty wc-product-gallery-slider-active vamtam-font-smoothing layout-full elementor-default elementor-kit-5 elementor-page elementor-page-9112
/research/dubai-residential-market-revie.intro: This review examines supply, absorption, and pricing across Dubai's prime and mid-market communities. With cross-border demand still robust and delivery pipelines normalising, we assess where yields and capital values are likely to hold — and where selectivity matters most for investors entering at this stage of the cycle.
takeaways: Prime communities continue to command premium pricing, though momentum is moderating from recent peaks.
Mid-market segments offer more attractive rental yields and steadier absorption for income-focused buyers.
Cross-border and NRI demand remains a key driver of transaction volumes across ready and off-plan stock.
New supply is normalising, making location, developer track record, and handover timelines increasingly decisive.

/research/india-real-estate-outlook-2026.desc: Where Valunxt sees value across India's residential and commercial real estate markets in 2026.
/research/india-real-estate-outlook-2026.body: wp-singular page-template-default page page-id-9111 page-parent wp-custom-logo wp-embed-responsive wp-theme-execor full header-layout-logo-menu no-page-header no-middle-header responsive-layout vamtam-is-elementor elementor-active elementor-pro-active vamtam-wc-cart-empty wc-product-gallery-slider-active vamtam-font-smoothing layout-full elementor-default elementor-kit-5 elementor-page elementor-page-9111
/research/india-real-estate-outlook-2026.intro: Our India Real Estate Outlook 2026 sets out where we see value across the country's residential and commercial markets. As rates ease and end-user demand stays resilient, we expect selective opportunities in Tier 1 metros and fast-growing corridors — supported by improving transparency, formalisation, and a maturing capital market.
takeaways: Residential demand remains structurally strong, led by end-users and upgraders across the top eight metros.
Grade-A office and warehousing continue to attract institutional capital on the back of steady rental growth.
Tier 2 corridors and emerging micro-markets offer attractive entry pricing for patient, research-led capital.
Regulatory formalisation and improving transparency are widening the investable universe for domestic and NRI investors.

/research/insights-2026/.title: Insights 2026: View on Real Estate and Infrastructure | Valunxt
/research/insights-2026/.desc: How Real Estate and Infrastructure are becoming increasingly attractive sources of resilient, inflation-protected returns as valuations stabilise and capital constraints persist.
/research/insights-2026/.body: wp-singular page-template-default page page-id-9110 page-parent wp-custom-logo wp-embed-responsive wp-theme-execor full header-layout-logo-menu no-page-header no-middle-header responsive-layout vamtam-is-elementor elementor-active elementor-pro-active vamtam-wc-cart-empty wc-product-gallery-slider-active vamtam-font-smoothing layout-full elementor-default elementor-kit-5 elementor-page elementor-page-9110
/research/insights-2026/.hero_title: Insights 2026: View on Real Estate and Infrastructure
/research/insights-2026/.intro: In Insights 2026, we highlight how Real Estate and Infrastructure are increasingly attractive sources of resilient, inflation-protected returns as valuations stabilise and capital constraints persist. Current market dislocation is creating compelling entry points for experienced managers, while long-term demand for digital infrastructure and power assets supports durable cash flows and return potential.
takeaways: Real Estate and Infrastructure provide inflation protection and downside resilience through hard assets and contracted income.
Slower fundraising and reduced transaction volumes are creating opportunities to invest at wider cap rates and on favourable terms.
Digital infrastructure and power assets benefit from strong secular tailwinds driven by AI, data growth and rising electricity demand.
Our priorities include partnering with experienced opportunistic managers, expanding value-add and middle-market exposure, and driving fee discounts and co-investments.

/research/nri-investment-trends/.title: NRI Investment Trends | Valunxt
/research/nri-investment-trends/.desc: How Non-Resident Indians are allocating to real estate across India and the UAE — markets, ticket sizes, and structuring.
/research/nri-investment-trends/.body: wp-singular page-template-default page page-id-9113 page-parent wp-custom-logo wp-embed-responsive wp-theme-execor full header-layout-logo-menu no-page-header no-middle-header responsive-layout vamtam-is-elementor elementor-active elementor-pro-active vamtam-wc-cart-empty wc-product-gallery-slider-active vamtam-font-smoothing layout-full elementor-default elementor-kit-5 elementor-page elementor-page-9113
/research/nri-investment-trends/.intro: Drawing on our client activity across India and the UAE, this note tracks how Non-Resident Indians are allocating to real estate back home. We look at preferred markets, ticket sizes, structuring choices, and the practical considerations — from due diligence to repatriation — that shape cross-border decisions.
takeaways: NRIs continue to favour Grade-A residential in familiar metros, increasingly complemented by commercial exposure.
Average ticket sizes are rising as investors consolidate into fewer, higher-quality assets.
Remote due diligence, transparent documentation, and trusted local partners are decisive for confidence.
Tax-aware structuring and clarity on repatriation remain central to how cross-border allocations are made.
